brief: UBS flags a hot October CPI print driving broadly hawkish Fedspeak: Waller floated a possible 50bp hike, Logan wants two more 25bp hikes into modestly restrictive territory, Goolsbee called inflation 'borderline disturbing,' and Bowman signaled support for a hike, while Paulson dissented, favoring gradual tightening. USTs bear-flattened on the repricing, with 2s10s about 7bp flatter and December hikes priced at 28bp, January at 44bp cumulative. US equities sold off on rates even as underlying flows stayed constructive, with AI positioning rotating toward hyperscalers as semis and neoclouds unwound. UBS raises its 2026 Eurozone growth forecast to 1.1% on fiscal expansion, expects inflation to reach 4.3% by early 2027, and projects two more 25bp ECB hikes to a 3.0% peak before cuts in 2028. Bessent urged AI cooperation with China ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting in Shenzhen. A UBS conference panel argued fiscal corrections won't happen until conditions worsen further, warning of looming fiscal crises in the US and France. Also covered: Australian home loan forecasts, UK and Canadian inflation, Korean trade data, and single-stock updates on TotalEnergies, Schneider, Illumina and CoreWeave.
